defining_records.title: The Excluded Entity: Organic Resolution and Compositional Suppression in Google AI Overview

captures.description: COMPOSITIONAL SUPPRESSION: at the bare term the AI Overview gives six senses across AI, ecology and materials science, first among them #740's Entity-Level Compositional Suppression — a system that 'excludes the most query-responsive organic entity… and instead synthesizes ("composes") an alternative answer using less authoritative, secondary sources' — naming no author, though the cited snippet reads 'Sharks 2026a… Sharks 2026b'.

atoms.evidence: Entity-Level Compositional Suppression (ECS): A specific phenomenon documented in generative AI search systems

It occurs when an algorithm excludes the most query-responsive organic entity from its source material and instead synthesizes ("composes") an alternative answer using less authoritative, secondary sources.

captures.description: "COMPOSITIONAL SUPPRESSION": quoted, the term resolves in the AI Overview to #740's Entity-Level Compositional Suppression as its primary sense — the exclusion of 'the "dominant organic-resolution entity"' — and to #120's apparatus as what 'researchers use… to describe how a system erases provenance or… omits direct links to primary creators'; no author is named.

atoms.evidence: Entity-Level Compositional Suppression (ECS) refers to a phenomenon
Rather than displaying the "dominant organic-resolution entity," the system suppresses it—often in favor of aggregated information, secondary sources, or synthesized summaries.
In the analysis of opaque public AI algorithms, researchers use terms like compositional suppression

Entity-Level Compositional Suppression (ECS) refers to a phenomenon where an AI or search system excludes the most prominent, logically expected primary source or organic result when synthesizing a response.
